text:
kevin: Heads-up — customer cust-8234 (Acme) reports large latency and billing hits. They claim requests pinned to eu-west-1 are getting routed to hosted pools in us-east-1. Example: tokens billed to hosted-gpu instead of dedicated-eu-01. Seeing intermittent 502s too. Can SRE/infra triage?

maya: Can you paste a failing request + gateway response and any request_id you have? Also need customer org id. thx

kevin: sample curl and response from the customer's repro: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer SK_REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"hello"}'
```
Response body we got: 
```
{"request_id":"r-0a1b2c","route":"us-east-1-hosted","status":"200","latency_ms":420}
```
Gateway log snippet around that request: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:04:12Z] route_decision request_id=r-0a1b2c customer=cust-8234 pinned_region=eu-west-1 route=us-east-1-hosted reason=dedicated_ineligible
[2026-03-15T10:04:12Z] billing_assign request_id=r-0a1b2c pool=hosted-us-east-1 tokens=128
```
Customer also attached a screenshot of their billing showing tokens charged under "hosted" pools for the same timeframe.

maya: weird. pinned_region is set but we fell back to hosted in a different continent. @raj can you check routing-service and pin-map TTLs? any recent deploys that touched pin logic?

raj: looking now. I can already see an anomalous spike in dedicated-eu-01's overflow counter. Pulling logs for routing-service v2.14.0 (deployed 03/14).

autoscale-bot: ALERT: dedicated-eu-01 overflow_rate=42r/m, queued=310, spill_rate=39r/m -> engaged fallback policy.

raj: OK here's the root cause summary so far: a bad parsing change in v2.14.0 changed pin TTL handling for legacy pin records. Some pins created before the deploy are being interpreted as expired (TTL parsed as ms vs s), so customers appear unpinned and the router treats them as ineligible for dedicated. Separately, the fallback selection logic was also regressing: when a pin is missing we should prefer same-region hosted fallback (eu-west hosted pools) but a recent change prioritized lowest-cost pool globally and picked us-east-hosted. That explains cross-continent routing + billing mismatch.

liam: Oof. So two parts: pins being dropped + fallback picking wrong region. What's the mitigation plan?

raj: Mitigations: 
1) Immediate hotfix: enable the feature-flag to force strict-region pin enforcement (routing.pin.strict_region=true) so router will refuse non-local fallbacks for pinned requests. This will reduce cross-region billing but may increase 503s if local capacity is exhausted.
2) Purge and rehydrate pin-map for affected customers (cust-8234 and a few others) to correct TTL units. Command: 
```
kubectl exec -n infra deployment/routing-service -- /routerctl purge-pins --customer cust-8234
```
3) Roll a small patch to v2.14.1 that fixes TTL parsing and fallback preference, then can safely disable the feature-flag.

maya: sounds good. @liam can you run 1+2? And please capture metrics before/after (latency, spill_rate, billing pool assignments).

liam: on it. Patching feature flag now and purging pin for cust-8234. Running: 
```
# set feature flag
kubectl -n infra exec deployment/routing-service -- /routerctl set-flag routing.pin.strict_region true
# purge bad pin
kubectl exec -n infra deployment/routing-service -- /routerctl purge-pins --customer cust-8234
```

liam: purge completed, restarted 3 router pods to pick up flag. Monitoring...

(10m later)

liam: observed immediate change: subsequent requests for cust-8234 now route to dedicated-eu-01. latency back to ~48ms. spill_rate for dedicated-eu-01 dropped to 2r/m. Billing pipeline shows new tokens attributed to dedicated-eu-01 for the next billing window.

kevin: passing this to the customer — they confirm lower latency and that numbers look normal in dashboard. They had screenshots showing spikes; I'll ask them to confirm there's no more hosted-billing.

maya: please open an operations incident and a GH bug. Assign to @raj for patch + postmortem. We need: repro steps, failing config diff, affected customers list, rollback window. Also add e2e test to catch TTL unit mismatch.

raj: created GH issue #4123 and a rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4125. Adding unit + integration tests for pin TTL and fallback selection.

kevin: thanks everyone. i'll note the customer follow-up and request 48h monitoring window.

maya: closing loop — good fast triage. please add postmortem doc once PR merged. :thumbsup:
